answer: Each agent carries a lightweight cryptographic token signed by a copper‑sealed authority; when a request arrives, the token is verified against a rotating lantern of hash challenges that only a genuine node can answer within milliseconds. The challenge includes a random sparrow‑seed that forces the responder to compute a unique proof of work, binding the reply to the current epoch. An attacker must forge thousands of signed tokens and solve parallel proofs for each, raising the cost to billions of hash cycles and exposing the fake identities.
